1: """``repo_wide`` marker invariant (#8707).
2: 
3: The selected CI tier picks test files by import-graph candidates: the Changes
4: job maps a changed ``scripts/foo.py`` to ``tests/**/test_foo*.py`` and a changed
5: ``tests/test_x.py`` to itself. A test that scans the repository's own trees has
6: no such import link, so selection can never pick it. That is how PR #8692
7: merged green on the selected tier and then turned ``main`` red:
8: ``tests/test_lint_test_assertions.py::test_repo_test_suite_is_clean`` scans all
9: of ``tests/`` for hard-coded epic assertions and was never selected for a
10: ``tests/orchestration/test_thread_handoff.py`` change.
11: 
12: Every test that enforces a repository-wide invariant by scanning files it does
13: not import must therefore carry ``repo_wide``, and the selected tier always
14: runs the marker (``ci.yml`` adds a ``-m repo_wide`` invocation). The docs lane
15: runs it too, because several repo-wide tests read ``docs/``. This module is
16: itself ``repo_wide``.
17: 
18: Two checks keep the marker honest:
19: 
20: 1. **The registry is the guarantee.** ``KNOWN_REPO_WIDE_MODULES`` and
21:    ``KNOWN_REPO_WIDE_FUNCTIONS`` are the authoritative list of whole-tree
22:    scanners. New scanners must be added there and marked; the registry checks
23:    fail if an entry disappears or loses its marker.
24: 2. **The heuristic is a best-effort net.** It parses each test module's AST and
25:    flags test functions that walk a repository source tree (a repo-root path
26:    expression joined to ``.rglob()``/``.glob()``, ``os.walk``/``os.scandir``,
27:    ``git ls-files``/``ls-tree`` through ``subprocess``, or a known whole-tree
28:    linter) and then propagates to callers of a scanning helper. It only finds
29:    what it was taught to look for; the registry, not the heuristic, is the
30:    correctness anchor. A genuinely repository-rooted scanner that is *not*
31:    repo-wide (a content reader, a top-level launcher glob whose only possible
32:    changes already force the full tier, and so on) is listed in
33:    ``NOT_REPO_WIDE`` with a reason.
34: 
35: Marker detection is syntactic and per-function: a test counts as marked only
36: when its own ``@pytest.mark.repo_wide`` decorator, its class decorator, or a
37: module-level ``pytestmark`` containing ``pytest.mark.repo_wide`` applies to it.
38: A comment or docstring mentioning the word does not count, and decorator order
39: is irrelevant.

83: ## Repo-wide tests always run in the selected and docs tiers (#8707)
84: 
85: Import selection can never pick a test that scans the repository's own trees:
86: the Changes job links a changed `scripts/foo.py` to `tests/**/test_foo*.py` (and
87: a changed `tests/test_x.py` to itself), but a test scanning `tests/` or
88: `scripts/` has no import edge to the changed module. That is how PR #8692
89: merged green on the selected tier and then turned `main` red on shard 3 for
90: every full-tier run: `tests/test_lint_test_assertions.py::test_repo_test_suite_is_clean`
91: scans all of `tests/` and was never selected for a `tests/orchestration/test_thread_handoff.py`
92: change.
93: 
94: Such tests carry the `repo_wide` marker (registered in `pyproject.toml`). After
95: the candidate run, a `selected` shard runs the marked set under its own narrow
96: allowlist:
97: 
98: ```
99: git ls-files -- tests | grep -E '/test_[^/]+\.py$' \
100:   | xargs -r grep -lE 'pytest\.mark\.repo_wide' | sort
101: LU_PYTEST_SHARD_FILES=<that list> pytest tests \
102:   -m 'repo_wide and not slow and not atlas_release' -n logical --dist=loadfile ...
103: ```
104: 
105: The narrow allowlist keeps collection cheap (the full tree is ~2 minutes to
106: collect); the known set currently runs ~400 tests in under two minutes. An
107: empty list fails the step loudly. The grep matches the exact marker
108: declaration, not a bare `repo_wide` mention, so a comment or an unrelated
109: string cannot pull a file into the allowlist (the `-m` filter would skip it
110: anyway, but the list stays honest).
111: 
112: The **docs lane** runs the same `-m repo_wide` invocation after its
113: `docs_skills` run. Docs-lane PRs reach no other pytest leg, and several
114: repo-wide scanners read `docs/`: `tests/test_work_privacy.py`,
115: `tests/test_agent_fleet_tooling_guardrails.py`, and
116: `tests/test_public_tree_no_baked_host_run_root.py`. A docs-only PR that adds a
117: baked host path under `docs/` is therefore caught before merge.
118: 
119: The **content lane** is deliberately unchanged. Every repo-wide test that reads
120: a content tree also carries `reads_content`, so `-m 'reads_content and not slow
121: and not atlas_release'` already runs it: `tests/test_llm_reviewer_dispatch.py`,
122: `tests/test_threshold_source_of_truth.py`, `tests/test_sparse_collection_guard.py`,
123: `tests/test_public_tree_no_baked_host_run_root.py`,
124: `tests/api/test_app_factory.py`, and
125: `tests/test_curriculum_upgrade_no_host_run_root.py` are all marked both ways,
126: and none is `slow`/`atlas_release`.
127: 
128: `tests/test_repo_wide_marker_invariant.py` keeps the marker honest. Marker
129: detection is syntactic and per-function (AST): a test counts only when its own
130: `@pytest.mark.repo_wide` decorator, its class decorator, or a module-level
131: `pytestmark` contains `pytest.mark.repo_wide`, so decorator order and comments
132: do not matter and a module with two scanners and one marker fails. The
133: authoritative guarantee is the explicit registry of known repo-wide
134: modules/functions plus a reasoned `NOT_REPO_WIDE` escape hatch; the AST
135: heuristic over each test module (repo-rooted `.glob`/`.rglob`,
136: `os.walk`/`os.scandir`, `git ls-files`/`ls-tree` through `subprocess`, and
137: known whole-tree linters, propagated through helper calls) is a best-effort
138: net. The invariant also fails when the selected tier or the docs lane drops
139: its `-m repo_wide` invocation.
140: 
141: No CF attest. No auto-arm. No landing-class classifier. No coverage floor.
142: Red team review is out of band.
